# Build your brand and grow on Amazon

Connect product sourcing, brand creation and marketplace operations through one coordinated plan. Ecomtik helps businesses prepare for launch, improve their Amazon presence and plan international expansion from its base in Dubai.

[Discuss your growth priorities](/contact) · [Explore our services](/services)

## Start with the challenge in front of you

**Launching a product:** Bring product research, suppliers, packaging, brand preparation and launch tasks into a clear sequence. [Explore private-label launch support](/services/amazon-private-label).

**Growing an existing Amazon business:** Review advertising, product content and operational priorities together. Understand what needs attention and who will own the work. [Explore Amazon account management](/services/amazon-account-management).

**Entering another marketplace:** Compare demand, local requirements, fulfilment and product economics before committing to expansion. [Explore marketplace expansion](/services/global-marketplace-expansion).

## Services that connect the product to the customer

Amazon management brings catalogue, advertising and reporting responsibilities into an agreed operating scope. Dedicated [PPC management](/services/amazon-ppc-management) and [listing optimisation](/services/amazon-listing-optimization) engagements can address a specific performance problem.

[Product sourcing](/services/amazon-product-sourcing) helps organise supplier evidence, specifications and cost comparisons. [Brand identity](/services/logo-design), [packaging](/services/product-packaging-design) and [ecommerce websites](/services/website-design) turn the product proposition into a consistent customer experience.

[Business setup coordination](/services/company-setup) supports the relevant formation process when the business needs it. The proposal separates formation work, third-party decisions and ongoing responsibilities.

## How a project moves forward

**Discover:** Review the business, products, market and immediate obstacles. Define the decision or outcome the engagement should support.

**Plan:** Agree deliverables, responsibilities, dependencies and a measurement approach. Identify the information needed before execution.

**Build and launch:** Complete the agreed tasks with review points for content, product and operational decisions.

**Measure and improve:** Review results against the starting position. Keep a record of changes and use the evidence to choose the next priorities.

## A clear scope before work begins

Your proposal should explain the work included, the inputs needed from your team and any external charges. You should know who owns the accounts and assets, how progress will be reviewed and what happens at handover.

## Practical guidance for Amazon sellers

Learn [why ACOS rises](/blog/high-amazon-acos), [what to check when a listing is suppressed](/blog/amazon-listing-suppressed), and [how to prepare an international launch](/blog/amazon-international-expansion).

## Tell us where your business needs support

Share your target marketplace, product or store link, and the main challenge you want to solve. We will use that context to discuss a suitable scope.

[Discuss your project](/contact)

# Amazon UAE launch and growth support

Plan Amazon.ae around the product, business documentation and customer experience you can actually deliver. An existing seller may need an account review, while a new brand needs a sequence for product preparation and launch.

## Prepare the local buying experience

Review how UAE customers describe and compare the product in relevant Arabic and English searches. Use a competent language reviewer for product facts and claims. Translation should preserve dimensions, compatibility and pack quantity without inventing benefits.

Check the delivered offer, fulfilment route and returns responsibilities. Model the product's actual economics in the operating currency, including the relevant marketplace charges and applicable tax treatment. The current Amazon UAE seller entrypoint is the starting source for local registration and programme information.[^A26]

## Agree the launch scope

A readiness engagement can organise registration inputs, catalogue information, inventory responsibilities, creative tasks and advertising preparation. An existing-account engagement can begin with the main constraint: visibility, conversion, cost or operations.

Ecomtik's base in Dubai supports its global positioning; the project still needs a named owner and agreed service scope. Business setup requirements and tax questions depend on the seller's circumstances and should be reviewed with the appropriate professional.

Bring your product category, store link if available, current stage and intended fulfilment plan to the first conversation. [Discuss Amazon UAE support](/contact) or explore [Amazon account management](/services/amazon-account-management).

# Amazon Saudi Arabia expansion support

Expanding to Amazon.sa needs a Saudi-specific readiness review. A successful UAE offer can provide useful learning, but it does not establish the requirements, buying language or economics of the same product in Saudi Arabia.

## Review the seller route and product

Check current seller eligibility and required documentation through Amazon Saudi Arabia's official seller information.[^A27] Review applicable product and import requirements with a suitable specialist before committing stock. Avoid treating a single regional checklist as approval for every category.

## Make the product clear in Arabic

Prepare a local keyword and customer-question brief. Review Arabic copy for accurate meaning, useful specifications and the way customers compare alternatives. Keep images, packaging and catalogue facts consistent. Confirm who will support language-dependent operational questions after launch.

## Build the destination cost and stock plan

Use destination-specific charges, transport assumptions, return arrangements and relevant taxes. Record the source and date for each cost input. Set responsibilities for stock, pricing, product updates and account notifications before launch.

A pilot product group can make the first release easier to evaluate. Agree the evidence needed to expand the catalogue and the conditions that would pause the rollout. This is a planning recommendation rather than a promised sales result.

[Discuss your Saudi marketplace plan](/contact) and review [international marketplace expansion](/services/global-marketplace-expansion).

[^A27]: Amazon. [Amazon Saudi Arabia official seller information](https://sell.amazon.sa/)

# Amazon US launch and expansion support

An Amazon.com launch should begin with the product's competitive position and destination economics. Compare the customer's alternatives, the real cost of delivery and the operational requirements before choosing the catalogue or ad budget.

## Start with the business you actually operate

Confirm the supported seller route for your business and location. A US LLC is not a universal requirement for international sellers to reach Amazon.com customers.[^A21] Formation, banking and marketplace approval are separate decisions. If formation is appropriate, agree its purpose and continuing responsibilities with suitable professional support.

## Prepare the product and offer

Review the category, applicable product requirements, English buying language and customer expectations. Confirm product identifiers, brand evidence and product facts before building the catalogue. Prepare a fulfilment and returns plan with identifiable owners.

Model the net price, inventory, logistics, relevant fees, expected returns and advertising in a consistent currency. Use current inputs for the product. A competitor's selling price alone does not establish an affordable launch.

## Launch with a defined review point

Choose an initial catalogue your team can support. Record the assumptions behind demand and advertising, then review actual contribution, stock and customer issues before expanding. Keep changes documented so learning from the launch remains usable.

[Discuss Amazon US expansion](/contact) or explore [Amazon brand launch support](/services/amazon-brand-launch).

[^A21]: Amazon. [Amazon selling to US customers from another country](https://sell.amazon.com/global-selling/international-to-usa)

# Amazon UK launch and expansion support

Prepare Amazon.co.uk as a distinct operating market. Product content, delivery, returns and business obligations need a UK-specific review rather than an unchanged copy of a US or European launch.

## Confirm the operating route

Review current account and programme eligibility and the product's requirements. Amazon's international guidance provides a starting point for expansion planning.[^A19] Use qualified advice for applicable tax, customs and product obligations. UK and EU requirements should not be treated as interchangeable.

## Build a clear local offer

Review the language UK customers use, appropriate measurements and product compatibility. Make pack size and included items clear. Prepare a returns arrangement and a stock plan that reflect the intended fulfilment route.

Compare expected net sales with product cost, transport, marketplace charges, returns and advertising. Keep currency assumptions explicit. A price copied from another Amazon store can create an offer that is uncompetitive or uneconomic.

## Separate company formation from marketplace launch

If a UK company is part of the chosen structure, review Companies House identity-verification requirements for the actual directors and people with significant control. Timing depends on the role and event.[^R04] Incorporation itself does not guarantee a bank account or seller approval.

Agree the catalogue, content, operational owners and launch review before committing to wider rollout. [Discuss Amazon UK support](/contact) or explore [international marketplace expansion](/services/global-marketplace-expansion).

[^A19]: Amazon. [Amazon Global Selling](https://sell.amazon.com/global-selling)

[^R04]: gov.uk. [When Companies House identity verification is required](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/when-you-need-to-verify-your-identity-for-companies-house)

# Amazon account management with a clear plan for growth

Your Amazon business depends on more than advertising. Listings, stock availability, pricing and account operations all affect what happens after a shopper finds your product. Ecomtik helps you connect those decisions through a defined management scope and an agreed set of priorities.

Start with the marketplace, products and problems that matter to your business. We review the current position, identify the most important gaps and agree who owns each action. The working plan should make it clear which tasks Ecomtik handles, which need your approval and which require a specialist.

You keep ownership of your seller account and commercial decisions. Reporting should explain what changed, why it changed and what the results mean for the next decision. Sales growth is evaluated alongside advertising spend, stock and product economics so an attractive headline does not hide a margin problem.

## What the engagement can include

- Initial catalogue, advertising and operational priorities review
- Written scope by marketplace and product group
- Action plan with owners, dependencies and approval points
- Agreed reporting covering sales, advertising and operational issues
- Regular planning reviews and a documented change log

## What we need to begin

Your marketplace, store or ASIN links, main constraints and business objectives. Any account access is arranged through appropriate user permissions after scope is agreed.

## Scope and responsibilities

Advertising spend, inventory, creative production and specialist account-recovery work are included only when specified in the proposal.

## Common questions

### Can I keep control of my account?

Yes. Your business should own its account and approve agency access through the available permission system. Avoid sharing your primary login.

### Can management guarantee higher sales?

No. The scope defines work and measurement. Demand, pricing, stock, competition and marketplace decisions also influence the result.

# Amazon PPC management built around your product economics

More advertising spend is useful only when it supports a clear business goal. Ecomtik helps you review where the budget goes, which searches turn into orders and whether the result works for your products and margins.

We begin with the current campaign structure, retail readiness and your commercial targets. A launch campaign, a mature product and a product with limited stock need different decisions. The plan should make those differences visible before bids or budgets change.

Reporting connects advertising results to total sales and contribution. ACOS is one useful measure, but it cannot explain profitability on its own. We look at search-term relevance, conversion, product availability and agreed objectives so decisions have a reason behind them.

## What the engagement can include

- Campaign and search-term assessment
- Product-specific targets and budget guardrails
- Campaign structure and targeting plan
- Search-term, bid and negative-target reviews
- Reporting with consistent dates, currency and attribution context

## What we need to begin

Target marketplaces, product margins, advertising objectives, stock constraints and relevant account reports through agreed access.

## Scope and responsibilities

Media spend is separate from the management fee. DSP, AMC, video production and non-Amazon advertising need an explicit scope.

## Common questions

### What is a good ACOS?

It depends on your product's contribution margin and campaign objective. A generic industry percentage is not a substitute for your own economics.

### Should every campaign use the same target?

Not necessarily. Brand defence, product launch and mature-product growth can have different roles. Targets should be explicit and reviewed.

# Amazon listings that answer the shopper's real questions

A shopper needs to understand what your product does, whether it fits their needs and why they should choose it. Ecomtik helps turn product information into clear, accurate listing content with a sensible search strategy.

The review starts with the product, its audience and the current listing. We separate visibility problems from conversion problems, then identify missing information, confusing images or weak purchase reasons. Relevant keywords are used where they support a useful explanation.

A content brief connects the title, bullets, image sequence and eligible A+ modules. Claims should be supported and product details consistent. Where the brand and products qualify, an experiment can compare content variants; a change should be measured against a defined question.

## What the engagement can include

- Search-intent and product-information review
- Title, bullet and description recommendations
- Image sequence and creative brief
- A+ content scope where eligible
- Implementation review and a measurement plan

Product specifications, approved claims, image rights, customer questions and relevant listing data.

## Scope and responsibilities

Photography, video, translation and A+ production are quoted separately unless included. Programme eligibility and content approval remain subject to Amazon.

## Common questions

### Is adding more keywords enough?

No. The listing must remain accurate and useful. Images, offer quality, stock and the product itself also influence purchases.

### Can every listing use A+ content or experiments?

Access depends on the current programme requirements and product eligibility. We check this before including the work.

# Product sourcing with clearer specifications and costs

The lowest factory quotation is only one part of a sourcing decision. Product quality, packaging, freight, delivery reliability and the destination market can change the economics. Ecomtik helps you organise those decisions before you commit to a production order.

A sourcing project starts with a usable product brief: materials, dimensions, performance, packaging and the requirements of your target market. Suppliers should respond to the same specification so their offers can be compared. Samples and inspection arrangements are agreed before a shipment decision.

The aim is a documented decision, with open questions visible. A landed-cost model should distinguish estimates from confirmed charges and account for the route to your intended warehouse. You approve the supplier and commercial commitment based on the evidence available.

## What the engagement can include

- Product brief and supplier comparison criteria
- Supplier outreach and quotation comparison within agreed scope
- Sample coordination and approval record
- Landed-cost assumptions and dependency review
- Quality-control and shipment handoff plan

## What we need to begin

Product concept or specification, destination market, target order size, timing and budget constraints.

## Scope and responsibilities

Manufacturing, samples, laboratory tests, inspection, freight, duties and insurance are separate third-party costs unless expressly included. State whether inspection is performed or coordinated.

## Common questions

### Can you work with a supplier I already found?

A project can be scoped around comparing that supplier's proposal, coordinating samples or improving the specification. The scope is agreed first.

### Does a sample guarantee the production order?

No. An approved sample is a reference. Production controls, inspection and clear purchase terms are separate safeguards.

# Build a private label product through clear decision stages

Launching your own brand brings more control and more responsibility. Ecomtik helps you connect the product opportunity, supplier decision, brand identity and marketplace plan before you place a major order.

Begin with a reason for the product to exist. Customer needs, competitive alternatives and unit economics should shape the concept before design or production. Each stage should resolve a practical question: is the product worth testing, is the sample suitable, can the offer support its costs, and is the business ready to launch?

A smaller first batch can help test an idea when the supplier and product allow it. We use micro private label to describe a smaller project scope, not a special Amazon programme or a guaranteed low-risk model. Fixed costs, minimum orders and working capital still matter.

## What the engagement can include

- Opportunity and differentiation brief
- Supplier and sample decision stages
- Brand, packaging and identifier readiness plan
- Product economics and launch budget assumptions
- Marketplace launch handoff and early review plan

Product idea, intended customer, target markets, available capital and any existing supplier or brand assets.

## Scope and responsibilities

Inventory purchases, trademark work, testing, logistics and advertising spend are separate unless specified. No product opportunity or sales outcome is guaranteed.

## Common questions

### What is micro private label?

It is a proposed smaller test scope for suitable products. The term does not remove compliance, quality or cash-flow responsibilities.

### Can I launch now and decide the brand later?

Plan the branding and product identifiers before listing. Generic and branded listings have different rules; a generic listing should not be treated as a simple route to later rebranding.

# Amazon wholesale decisions grounded in supply and margins

A wholesale opportunity needs more than a familiar brand name. Authentic supply, usable purchase evidence, selling permissions and offer competition all matter. Ecomtik helps you organise those checks before a buying decision.

The review connects the supplier, product and marketplace. Confirm what you are buying, whether the supplier can provide genuine documentation and what selling restrictions apply to the actual account and product. Then model the likely costs and price pressure.

A profitable-looking first order can still tie up cash if sales slow or the offer becomes less competitive. Build a replenishment and exit plan before scaling. Your records should show the assumptions behind a purchase and the conditions that would change the next order.

## What the engagement can include

- Supplier and product documentation checklist
- Product-level permission review plan
- Offer and competitive-price assessment
- Unit margin and replenishment assumptions
- Purchase-decision and follow-up action record

## What we need to begin

Supplier details, product identifiers, authentic invoices or quotations and target marketplace.

## Scope and responsibilities

Ecomtik does not create or alter supplier invoices. Supplier acceptance, brand permission and Amazon approval are separate decisions.

## Common questions

### Does an invoice guarantee approval?

No. Requirements depend on the product, marketplace and actual request. Keep genuine documents and check the current account instructions.

### Is wholesale the same as private label?

No. Wholesale resells existing branded products. Private label develops an offer under your own brand, with different costs and responsibilities.

# Prepare a clearer Amazon Brand Registry application

Brand Registry starts with the brand's rights and application evidence. Ecomtik helps you organise the information, check consistency and understand the next steps before you submit.

The review covers the brand name, trademark information, product or packaging evidence and who is authorised to act. An eligible registered or pending trademark may qualify under Amazon's current requirements. Eligibility should be checked against the relevant trademark office and application circumstances.

The rights owner should retain control and delegate access appropriately. Enrollment can provide access to useful brand tools, subject to their requirements, but it does not automatically make every other seller unauthorised or guarantee the outcome of a complaint.

## What the engagement can include

- Eligibility and application-readiness checklist
- Brand-name and evidence consistency review
- Submission coordination within agreed permissions
- Clarification and case-document organisation
- Handover explaining account roles and next steps

## What we need to begin

Trademark details, rights-owner information, brand assets and genuine product or packaging images.

## Scope and responsibilities

Trademark clearance, filing and legal enforcement require a qualified provider where applicable. Amazon decides enrollment and tool eligibility.

## Common questions

### Must my trademark already be fully registered?

Amazon accepts certain pending applications as well as registered marks. Check the current eligibility rules for the office and status involved.

### Does Brand Registry guarantee exclusive selling rights?

No. Enrollment and the assessment of a specific intellectual-property or policy complaint are different matters.

bodyMarkdown:
# Why your Amazon ACOS is high and what to check

A high advertising cost of sales, or ACOS, means advertising spend takes a large share of the sales attributed to those ads. Before lowering every bid, check whether the problem comes from expensive clicks, weak conversion or a target that does not fit the product's margin. Amazon defines ACOS as ad spend divided by ad-attributed sales, expressed as a percentage.[^A01]

## Calculate what the product can afford

Suppose an order produces $40 in net sales. Product cost, marketplace fees, fulfilment and an allowance for expected returns total $28. That leaves $12 before advertising and fixed overhead. In this simplified example, spending $12 to acquire the order uses the entire contribution. The corresponding ACOS is 30%. Spending $8 leaves $4 before fixed overhead, giving an ACOS of 20%.

These are illustrative figures, not a recommended target. Use your actual costs, treat taxes consistently and account for discounts and refunds. Repeat the calculation by product; an account average can hide products that lose money.

## Separate targeting from conversion

Export campaign and search-term data for a consistent period, allowing for the applicable reporting delay and attribution window. Review the actual shopper searches and product placements that spent money. Group them into relevant buyers, unclear intent and obvious mismatches. Negative targeting can help exclude unsuitable searches or products, but its scope depends on the campaign and targeting type.[^A02]

Then inspect the detail page. Is the advertised variation available? Does the main image communicate the product? Can a buyer understand size, compatibility and quantity? Is the delivered price competitive for the value offered? A bid change cannot repair inaccurate product information.

## Make one decision at a time

Build a short change log with the target, spend, attributed sales, reason for action and review date. Reduce exposure to confirmed mismatches. Give relevant but inconclusive targets a defined test budget based on what the business can afford to learn. Avoid a universal rule that every target must be paused after the same number of clicks.

For example, two targets could each spend $30 without a sale. One may be irrelevant to the product; the other may have too little evidence for a high-priced item. The same spend does not justify the same decision. Set limits deliberately and avoid extending a test indefinitely because you hope it will recover.

## Check the business result

Compare ACOS with total sales, contribution and inventory availability. TACOS is ad spend divided by total sales for the chosen scope and period. It provides another view of advertising dependence, but it does not prove that ads caused organic sales. Keep the currency and revenue definitions consistent.

Amazon's Sponsored Products guidance links advertising preparation with product-page readiness.[^A24] Review the offer before increasing spend, and judge changes over enough comparable data to avoid reacting to normal daily variation.

Need a structured review? Explore [Ecomtik's Amazon PPC management](/services/amazon-ppc-management). If shoppers already click but do not buy, continue with [the conversion checklist](/blog/amazon-clicks-no-sales).

[^A01]: Amazon. [Amazon Ads guide to ACOS](https://advertising.amazon.com/library/guides/acos-advertising-cost-of-sales)

[^A02]: Amazon. [Amazon Sponsored Products targeting guide](https://advertising.amazon.com/library/guides/targeting-with-sponsored-products)

[^A24]: Amazon. [Amazon review of Sponsored Products best practices](https://advertising.amazon.com/library/guides/sponsored-products-best-practices)

# Amazon listing suppressed and what to check first

If an Amazon listing is suppressed, begin with the issue Amazon shows for that product. A missing search result alone does not establish suppression. Search visibility, an inactive offer, unavailable stock and a policy restriction can require different actions.

Amazon provides a suppressed-listings help page, but the precise fields and instructions should be checked inside the affected marketplace's Seller Central account.[^A04] Avoid applying a generic fix before you know the reason.

## Identify the affected record

Record the marketplace, Amazon Standard Identification Number or ASIN, seller SKU, variation and time the issue appeared. Save the exact notice and any error code. Note recent changes to images, brand data, required attributes or inventory feeds. This gives you a useful starting point if the correction does not work immediately.

Check whether the problem affects one child variation, the parent relationship or several unrelated products. Do not assume that editing the parent will resolve every child record. Confirm which record the system actually identifies.

## Correct the stated problem

If the notice requests an attribute, verify the product fact and enter it in the required field. If it concerns imagery, compare the actual file with the current category requirements. If it concerns a product identifier or brand mismatch, check the source records before making another catalogue change.

Amazon's identifier guidance distinguishes a GTIN from an ASIN and a seller SKU.[^A11] Treat those as different records in your troubleshooting notes. Do not substitute invented identifiers or select generic branding simply to bypass an error. Amazon places restrictions on changes involving generic product branding.[^A12]

## Keep the evidence in one place

Use a simple log: affected SKU, exact error, evidence, field changed, submission time and observed result. If a corrected value later reverts, investigate feeds, integrations and other catalogue contributions before repeatedly submitting the same edit.

For illustration, a bottle listing might lack a required capacity value. The right action is to confirm the capacity against the product specification and update the named field. Rewriting the entire description and changing the brand at the same time would make the outcome harder to diagnose.

## Verify the customer view

After the applicable processing period, inspect both the account status and the customer-facing detail page. Check the correct marketplace and delivery location. Confirm the offer, relevant variation, images and required information. Save the result with a timestamp.

If the issue remains, use the support route shown in the account. Provide the precise error, the correction attempted and genuine supporting records. Ask a specific question about the unresolved discrepancy. Preserve the case reference so the next person can follow the history.

There is no universal restoration time. Continue monitoring and investigate related notifications where the account directs you. A successful edit submission and a restored customer offer are separate checks.

See [Ecomtik's listing optimisation scope](/services/amazon-listing-optimization) for catalogue and content support. For stock without an active offer, read [the FBA inventory guide](/blog/fba-stockouts-stranded-inventory).

[^A04]: Amazon. [Amazon suppressed listings help](https://sellercentral.amazon.com/help/hub/reference/external/G200898440)

[^A11]: Amazon. [Amazon product IDs and GTINs](https://sell.amazon.com/blog/amazon-gtin-guide)

[^A12]: Amazon. [Amazon guide to generic products](https://sell.amazon.com/blog/sell-generic-products)

# Amazon Featured Offer missing and what to review

The Featured Offer is the offer highlighted for purchase on an Amazon product page. Sellers often call it the Buy Box. Having an active listing does not mean your offer will be selected. Amazon's guide distinguishes eligibility from the competitive factors considered for selection.[^A03]

Start by checking the affected ASIN, marketplace, variation and delivery location. A screenshot without those details can send you towards the wrong diagnosis.

## Confirm that the offer is available

Check the seller account for offer status and any associated notifications. Confirm that the correct SKU has available stock and can be delivered to the destination being tested. A warehouse quantity is not necessarily the same as inventory available for customers to purchase.

For Fulfilment by Amazon, or FBA, inspect the relevant stock statuses. Amazon's FBA programme handles specified fulfilment activities, but the programme description is not a promise that every inbound unit is immediately available.[^A17]

## Compare the complete customer offer

Review the total delivered price, delivery expectation, product condition and customer service performance alongside the status information in your account. These are relevant considerations in Amazon's Featured Offer guidance.[^A03] Keep a record of when the comparison was made because offers can change.

Do not respond by automatically becoming the cheapest seller. First calculate the lowest price your business can support. A product that sells more units below its contribution threshold can create a larger cash problem.

## Build a short diagnosis record

Create columns for observation time, marketplace, ASIN, seller SKU, availability, delivered price, delivery estimate and relevant account notice. Add a final column for the action taken. This is an operating recommendation, not an Amazon-required format.

Imagine a seller reducing price while the product remains unavailable to the customer's location. The discount does not address the availability issue. Another seller may have stock and a competitive price but an unresolved performance notification. The account evidence should determine the next step in each case.

## Test changes within a margin limit

Where a price change is appropriate, record the original price, the reason for the test and the minimum acceptable contribution. Inspect the result over a comparable period and watch total contribution as well as offer visibility. Avoid changing price, fulfilment and advertising simultaneously unless an urgent operational issue requires it.

Keep account and catalogue notices in the same review. If you need support, send a precise description of the inconsistency rather than asking only why you have no Buy Box. Amazon controls eligibility and selection; no agency can promise permanent ownership of the placement.

For coordinated offer, catalogue and advertising work, review [Ecomtik's Amazon account management](/services/amazon-account-management). If paid traffic is reaching the page but orders remain weak, use [the clicks without sales checklist](/blog/amazon-clicks-no-sales).

bodyMarkdown:
# FBA stockouts and stranded inventory explained

An Amazon seller can run out of sellable stock while still owning inventory. Units may be in production, travelling to a warehouse, awaiting receipt or linked to an offer that is no longer active. The first useful action is to separate those situations.

Amazon describes stranded inventory as FBA stock that lacks an active offer. Its help page should be checked in the affected marketplace for the applicable correction options.[^A05] Ordering more units will not resolve that listing connection.

## Build an inventory view by SKU

For each seller SKU and marketplace, record sellable stock, inbound units, relevant reserved quantities, unfulfillable stock and stranded inventory. Add confirmed purchase orders separately. Avoid counting a shipment both as inbound stock and as a supplier commitment.

Assign a next action to every exception. A stranded item needs the offer issue investigated. A delayed shipment needs shipment evidence and a realistic receiving estimate. An unfulfillable item requires the relevant disposition review. Use the current account options rather than assuming the same action fits every status.

## Estimate when to reorder

A simple planning calculation is expected daily demand multiplied by total replenishment lead time, plus a safety allowance. Lead time should include production, inspection, transport and receiving assumptions, not only the supplier's promised dispatch date.

For illustration, demand of 8 units a day across a 45-day lead time requires 360 units. Adding a 90-unit buffer gives a 450-unit reorder point. This is a planning example, not an Amazon rule or a recommended buffer. Compare the trigger with your inventory position and confirmed supply, and adjust for seasonality and uncertainty.

A recent promotion may make average daily sales unsuitable for the next period. Document the period used, planned promotions and any changes to price or distribution. Review your forecast against actual demand so the buffer has a reason behind it.

## Connect the plan to cash

Before placing a reorder, list the deposit, balance payment, freight payment and expected availability date. The timing matters even if the product has a positive margin. More inventory can reduce stockout risk while creating excess storage cost or leaving too little cash for other products.

Amazon's FBA information describes fulfilment services and fee categories, but actual charges need the relevant marketplace and product details.[^A17] Use the current fee tools and your charged transactions when assessing an order.

## Hold a short weekly review

Review low-stock products, delayed inbound shipments, stranded items and slow-moving stock. Give each action a person and a review date. Keep an exception open until the account or physical evidence shows it is resolved. A message sent to a supplier is progress, not proof of receipt.

Need help understanding an inventory issue? [Discuss your situation with Ecomtik](/contact) and confirm the relevant service availability. Before buying another batch, revisit [your launch and working-capital budget](/blog/amazon-launch-budget).

[^A05]: Amazon. [Amazon fix stranded inventory help](https://sellercentral.amazon.com/gp/help/external/G201436600)

[^A17]: Amazon. [Fulfillment by Amazon](https://sell.amazon.com/fulfillment-by-amazon)

bodyMarkdown:
# How to check an Amazon supplier before ordering

A low quotation is only one part of a sourcing decision. Before sending a deposit, establish who you are buying from, what the supplier will deliver and how you will verify the order. Wholesale resale and private-label manufacturing need different checks.

Amazon's public wholesaler guide recommends supplier research and validation. Its branded-product guidance also highlights authentic sourcing and applicable selling permissions.[^A14][^A15] Check eligibility for the specific product before buying stock; a persuasive supplier presentation cannot establish marketplace approval.

## Verify the business relationship

Record the supplier's legal business name, contact details, location and payment beneficiary. Ask who manufactures the goods, who invoices the order and whether an intermediary is involved. Resolve mismatches through independent checks and genuine business documentation before proceeding.

For branded wholesale, request evidence of the legitimate supply chain and any relevant authorization. Preserve original invoices and communications. Do not edit a supplier document to make it appear to meet a requirement that the transaction did not satisfy.

## Write a product specification

Replace vague descriptions such as premium quality with observable requirements. Depending on the product, specify materials, dimensions, finish, quantity, packaging, markings and acceptable tolerances. Identify what needs specialist testing for the destination and who will commission it.

For example, two storage-box quotations may look comparable until one includes thicker material, individual packaging and carton labels while the other does not. A shared specification makes the difference visible before price negotiations.

## Inspect a representative sample

Keep a sample decision log with photographs, measurements, issues and approval conditions. Compare the sample against the written specification. Agree what happens if production differs and who has authority to approve a change.

A sample is evidence about that sample. It does not prove that every unit in a future batch will be identical. Set appropriate inspection checkpoints and engage a suitable independent provider when the product or order warrants it. If an agency coordinates inspection rather than performing it directly, its scope should say so.

## Compare landed cost and cash terms

Use a supplier comparison that includes unit cost, packaging, minimum order quantity, tooling, testing, inspection, freight assumptions and payment stages. Add duties, taxes and local handling where applicable with qualified support. Use the same currency and delivery basis for each option.

An illustrative quotation of $4 a unit may be more expensive in the final destination than a $4.40 alternative with different packaging and freight terms. Separate known amounts from estimates. Do not make a purchase decision from an attractive unit price with the other fields blank.

## Start with a controlled purchase decision

Summarise unresolved questions, the evidence received and the person approving the order. Choose a test quantity based on demand, cash and operational risk. A sourcing project should leave you with an understandable decision record.

Explore [Ecomtik's product sourcing service](/services/amazon-product-sourcing). For the wider cost picture, read [how to build an Amazon launch budget](/blog/amazon-launch-budget).

[^A14]: Amazon. [Amazon guide to finding wholesalers](https://sell.amazon.com/blog/how-to-find-wholesalers)

[^A15]: Amazon. [Amazon guide to selling branded products](https://sell.amazon.com/blog/sell-branded-products-on-amazon)

metadata.publicationRequirement: Assign reviewer and actual publication date

bodyMarkdown:
# How to build an Amazon launch budget

There is no single launch budget that fits every Amazon seller. A useful budget follows the product, marketplace and business model. Separate the cost of preparing the launch from the money required to replenish stock after it starts selling.

Private label means selling a product under your own brand, with responsibilities that extend beyond buying inventory.[^A13] Account registration also depends on the seller's circumstances and required business information.[^A18] Decide the operating model before choosing a headline budget.

## List the costs before calculating profit

Create separate lines for samples, design, product development, inventory, testing, inspection, packaging, transport and launch content. Add relevant registration or professional-service costs only where they apply. Distinguish a one-time cost from a recurring cost and a payment commitment from a rough estimate.

Then model each sale using the expected net selling price, product cost, applicable marketplace charges, fulfilment, returns allowance and advertising. Amazon's FBA fees depend on product and marketplace details; a US programme page is not a worldwide fee schedule.[^A17]

## Use a transparent example

Suppose net sales per unit are $30. Landed product cost is $9, marketplace and fulfilment charges are $8, and the allowance for expected returns and other variable costs is $1. This leaves $12 before advertising and fixed overhead. If advertising uses $6 per acquired order, contribution is $6.

If one-time launch costs total $1,800, then 300 units contributing $6 each would cover those launch costs in this simplified model. Inventory purchase cash is still needed upfront. The example assumes stable prices, costs and acquisition economics; it is not a profit forecast or an Amazon fee quote.

## Stress the assumptions

Recalculate with a lower selling price, slower sales, higher ad cost and additional freight. Change one driver at a time to see what matters. Then consider a combined difficult case. A small margin that disappears after a modest cost change deserves attention before a large order.

Record the evidence behind expected demand. A competitor's visible sales rank, a search trend or a supplier's estimate is only part of that assessment. Explain what has been validated and what the first purchase is intended to test.

## Build a payment calendar

Put deposits, production balances, shipping payments, advertising charges and expected settlements on a calendar. Add a possible reorder before the first batch has fully sold. Cash timing can create pressure even when the unit model is positive.

Keep a reserve that reflects the actual uncertainties. There is no universal buffer percentage. If the business cannot fund an unexpected delay or a reasonable reorder, reduce scope or reconsider the launch sequence.

Ecomtik's [private-label service](/services/amazon-private-label) can be scoped around research, sourcing, brand preparation and launch coordination. Start with [the supplier checklist](/blog/amazon-supplier-vetting) before treating any quotation as a committed launch cost.

[^A13]: Amazon. [Amazon private label products](https://sell.amazon.com/blog/private-label-products)

[^A18]: Amazon. [Amazon registration guide](https://sell.amazon.com/sell/registration-guide)

[^A17]: Amazon. [Fulfillment by Amazon](https://sell.amazon.com/fulfillment-by-amazon)

# Amazon Brand Registry preparation checklist

Before applying for Amazon Brand Registry, confirm the brand's eligibility and the rights holder. Amazon accepts qualifying registered trademarks and certain pending applications under its current requirements. The accepted trademark offices, statuses and application details must be checked for the actual case.[^A07][^A08]

An agency can help organise the application, but the brand owner should control the rights and account relationship. Brand Registry is not a substitute for trademark advice or a promise that every other seller will disappear.

## Create a consistent brand record

Write down the exact brand name, trademark reference, owner name and relevant application details. Compare those with the product and packaging. Resolve differences before submitting another variation of the same information.

For illustration, a packaging file might show one spelling while a trademark record uses another. Treat that as an evidence issue to investigate with the rights holder. Do not alter official records or digitally add a mark to photographs to make the application appear consistent.

## Gather genuine product evidence

Prepare clear, current photographs and supporting information requested by the application. Keep original files and record which products the evidence represents. Use actual products or packaging rather than a visual mockup presented as a manufactured item.

Coordinate the timing with the sourcing and packaging team. It is more efficient to identify a brand-evidence requirement before approving production artwork than to discover a mismatch after stock has shipped.

## Keep identifiers separate

A trademark, a GTIN, an ASIN and a seller SKU serve different purposes. Amazon's GTIN guide explains the product-identifier distinctions.[^A11] Make sure the person building the catalogue understands which record belongs in each field.

Do not assume that a generic listing can later become a branded listing by changing its name. Amazon's generic-product guidance imposes restrictions on that route.[^A12] Decide the genuine brand status early and investigate the correct catalogue path if an existing record is wrong.

## Agree access and responsibilities

Record who owns the brand account, who receives verification communications and which permissions an agency needs. Use permissioned access rather than sharing the owner's primary password. Agree who will maintain trademark information and handle future changes.

Create an application log containing the date, submitted information, requests for clarification and final response. If further evidence is requested, answer that request precisely and keep the history together. Repeated submissions with inconsistent details can make the case harder to follow.

## Plan what happens after approval

Review the programmes and tools available to the brand and its products. Availability can depend on marketplace, account and product eligibility. Set up a separate content and launch plan rather than treating enrollment itself as a sales strategy.

Read [Ecomtik's Brand Registry assistance scope](/services/brand-registry) for help with preparation. If the brand is still being developed, explore [the private-label launch service](/services/amazon-private-label).

[^A08]: Amazon. [Amazon Brand Registry requirements](https://sell.amazon.com/blog/brand-registry-requirements)

[^A12]: Amazon. [Amazon guide to generic products](https://sell.amazon.com/blog/sell-generic-products)

# Amazon ads get clicks but no sales and what to check

When shoppers click an Amazon ad but do not buy, investigate the customer journey before buying more traffic. The cause could be an unsuitable search, an unclear product page or an offer the shopper cannot purchase. A small number of clicks can also be inconclusive.

Begin with the affected product, variation, marketplace and a consistent reporting period. Allow for the applicable attribution window before deciding that every recent click produced no sale.

## Check who the ad is attracting

Review actual search terms and product placements. Compare the shopper's likely need with the product's real purpose, price and compatibility. Amazon's targeting guide explains keyword and product targeting, including options for excluding inappropriate traffic.[^A02]

For example, a premium stainless-steel bottle may attract searches for a cheap plastic party bottle. The word bottle is relevant at a broad level, but the intended purchase may be different. Confirm mismatches before excluding terms that could describe a valid customer.

## Inspect the buying experience

Open the detail page for the relevant delivery location. Verify availability, selected variation, delivered price and delivery expectation. Check whether the title, images and specifications describe the same product. A pack-size misunderstanding can stop a purchase even when the page looks attractive.

Ask someone unfamiliar with the product to explain what they would receive. Note where they hesitate. This is a practical usability exercise, not a replacement for measured conversion data.

## Answer the questions that block a purchase

List the facts a buyer needs: dimensions, materials, compatibility, what is included, setup and appropriate use. Prioritise the questions visible in genuine customer feedback and product enquiries. Improve the explanation without adding unsupported performance claims.

For illustration, a chair image can communicate style but leave seat height and assembly unclear. A readable dimension image and an accurate assembly explanation address those uncertainties. Adding more decorative graphics would not necessarily answer either question.

## Test a specific hypothesis

Write the proposed change, the reason it should help and the metric you will observe. Where eligible, Amazon's Manage Your Experiments supports testing specified listing content.[^A09] If a controlled experiment is unavailable, record other changes and compare periods carefully. A before-and-after result alone does not establish causation.

Avoid changing price, primary imagery, title and campaign structure together unless there is a clear operational reason. Otherwise, even a better result may leave you unable to identify which change mattered.

## Decide whether to scale

Connect conversion with contribution per order and available stock. A campaign can convert yet remain too expensive. Amazon's advertising guidance treats retail readiness as part of campaign preparation.[^A24] Use an affordable test budget and a review date; do not increase spend solely because click volume looks encouraging.

Explore [Ecomtik's listing optimisation and A+ content service](/services/amazon-listing-optimization). For the advertising economics, read [the high-ACOS guide](/blog/high-amazon-acos).

[^A02]: Amazon. [Amazon Sponsored Products targeting guide](https://advertising.amazon.com/library/guides/targeting-with-sponsored-products)

[^A09]: Amazon. [Amazon Manage Your Experiments](https://sell.amazon.com/tools/manage-your-experiments)

bodyMarkdown:
# Amazon account deactivated and how to organise a response

Start with the exact notice in your Amazon account. A deactivation may involve identity verification, product authenticity, performance, policy compliance or another stated issue. The response needs to address that issue and the instructions given for the account.

Amazon's account-health guidance is the official starting point.[^A06] Public seller discussions show that people can misunderstand the relationship between a health score and a particular enforcement action, but a forum account does not prove how another case will be decided.[^V03]

## Preserve the notice and records

Save the complete notification, relevant dates, affected products and the requested submission route. Keep genuine supplier records, transaction history and previous communications in a secure location. Record who has made recent changes to the account or catalogue.

Create a short timeline. Separate known facts from assumptions. If a document is missing, record that gap openly rather than filling it with a guessed date or an edited invoice.

## Define the issue in one sentence

Write a plain description of the problem Amazon has identified. Then list the evidence needed to answer it. If the notice requests a specific verification step, complete or investigate that step rather than immediately sending an unrelated appeal letter.

For illustration, a business-information mismatch calls for reconciliation of the actual records. A complaint about a product requires a different evidence review. The word suspended does not make those two tasks interchangeable.

## Fix what can be corrected

Where the facts establish an operational problem, document the correction and who is responsible for maintaining it. This might involve a purchasing check, a catalogue approval process or a change in document handling. Use measures that the business has actually implemented.

Do not promise controls that nobody owns. A statement that all suppliers will be checked is less useful than a defined purchasing checkpoint with evidence, responsibility and a review frequency appropriate to the business.

## Make the response easy to follow

Follow the format and channel requested in the account. Answer the stated issue, connect claims to genuine evidence and explain completed corrective work where relevant. Keep the response internally consistent. A generic template can omit the very fact that matters most.

Maintain one case log with submission dates, references, requests and responses. If the reply raises a new question, address it using the accumulated record. Avoid contradictory submissions from several people working independently.

## Prepare an operational contingency

Review affected stock, open commitments and communication responsibilities while the issue is unresolved. Decisions about funds, inventory or legal disputes depend on the actual account notice and circumstances. Use qualified specialist advice where needed.

No provider can promise reinstatement or a universal decision time. [Discuss an account-health review with Ecomtik](/contact) and confirm specialist availability and scope before commissioning support. For prevention at the purchasing stage, read [the supplier-verification guide](/blog/amazon-supplier-vetting).

bodyMarkdown:
# How to review FBA fees and reimbursement discrepancies

An unexpected FBA charge is a reason to investigate. It is not automatically an error or an entitlement to reimbursement. Start with the transaction, relevant product details and the policy that applies to that event in the marketplace.

Amazon's public FBA page introduces the programme and fee categories.[^A17] For an actual reconciliation, use the current detailed fee schedule and charged account data. Keep estimates separate from amounts already assessed.

## Reconcile one type of issue at a time

Separate fulfilment charges, storage charges, inbound discrepancies, customer returns and inventory reimbursement events. Each has different evidence and policy questions. A single total labelled Amazon owes us hides those differences.

For every potential discrepancy, record the marketplace, transaction date, SKU, ASIN, charged amount, reason for review and supporting reference. Preserve the original report. Put calculations and explanations in a separate working sheet so the source remains inspectable.

## Match evidence to the question

For a dimensional concern, compare the relevant packaged dimensions and weight with the charged classification and current rules. For a shipment concern, preserve the shipment references, quantities and genuine dispatch or receipt evidence. For a reimbursement event, identify the policy and valuation basis that applies.

Check for reversals, partial adjustments and earlier payments before opening another case. A reimbursement posted in a later period can otherwise look like an unresolved loss in the original report.

## Do not reuse outdated assumptions

An Amazon announcement in 2025 moved a manufacturing-cost reimbursement implementation date to 31 March 2025.[^A23] That historical announcement is a reason to verify the current policy, not a complete statement of every present reimbursement rule.

Confirm eligibility, evidence, valuation and submission timing for the specific event. Do not assume retail selling price is the correct reimbursement value. Avoid a universal claim deadline copied from an old blog or applied across unrelated event types.

## Keep a case calculation readable

Imagine a shipment of 120 units, a later record of 114 received units and a further adjustment of 4 units. The remaining quantity to investigate is 2, subject to the actual receiving and reconciliation status. Claiming 6 without incorporating the adjustment would overstate the discrepancy. These are illustrative quantities, not evidence of an Amazon case.

A case should show the source quantity, adjustments, remaining difference and evidence. Keep the original currency. Do not add speculative profit or unrelated costs unless the applicable policy expressly supports them.

## Close the loop

Track submitted, awaiting response, further evidence requested, adjusted and closed states. Close a case only after reconciling the outcome to the account. Use recurring issues to improve packaging records, shipment handoffs or document retention.

[Discuss a scoped FBA review with Ecomtik](/contact) and confirm specialist availability. For prevention through better stock records, read [the inventory planning guide](/blog/fba-stockouts-stranded-inventory).

[^A17]: Amazon. [Fulfillment by Amazon](https://sell.amazon.com/fulfillment-by-amazon)

[^A23]: Amazon. [Amazon inventory reimbursement update](https://sellercentral.amazon.com/seller-forums/discussions/t/ed8abc33-a1d5-417d-b2e2-03b789099833)

metadata.title: How to Build an Amazon Review Process Without Incentives
metadata.description: Improve product expectations and organise neutral review requests while avoiding paid reviews, selective requests and misleading inserts.
metadata.h1: How to build an Amazon review process without incentives
metadata.publicationRequirement: Assign reviewer and actual publication date

bodyMarkdown:
# How to build an Amazon review process without incentives

A review process should support honest feedback from real customers. Start by reviewing Amazon's current customer-review policy for your marketplace.[^A10] Do not offer money, refunds, gifts or other benefits in exchange for a favourable review. Do not ask only satisfied buyers for public feedback while directing dissatisfied buyers elsewhere.

The product and buying experience come first. A request cannot correct a misleading description or a recurring quality problem.

## Make product expectations accurate

Compare the listing with what arrives in the customer's package. Check quantity, size, colour, materials, compatibility and included accessories. Review genuine feedback for repeated misunderstandings. Correct the source of the confusion in product information, packaging or quality control.

For illustration, if buyers repeatedly expected two pieces but received one, the useful response is to clarify pack quantity throughout the listing and inspect why the images created that expectation. Asking for more positive reviews would leave the problem unresolved.

## Use a neutral request process

Use the review-request tools and routes currently permitted in the account. Confirm applicable timing and messaging rules before setting up automation. Keep the request neutral and avoid linking customer support, warranty assistance or a remedy to the review a person leaves.

Record which system sends requests so two tools do not contact the same buyer unnecessarily. Define who checks template wording after a policy change. A process that was once acceptable needs review when either the tool or the rules change.

## Review inserts and support messages

Inspect physical package inserts, automated emails and customer-service templates together. A compliant-looking account message does not solve an inappropriate request printed inside the box. Remove language that offers a benefit for a particular rating or asks someone to change feedback as a condition of receiving help.

Keep service recovery focused on the customer's actual problem. A refund, replacement or explanation should follow the applicable order and support process. The customer must remain free to give an honest account of their experience.

## Learn from recurring themes

Maintain an issue log using broad categories such as sizing, instructions, durability, missing parts and delivery damage. Record the product, underlying evidence, proposed correction and owner. Do not copy private customer information into public reports.

Compare complaint themes with returns, support contacts and inspection findings. If several sources point to the same assembly problem, improving instructions may help the customer experience across all of them. This is an operational hypothesis to evaluate, not a guaranteed method for increasing ratings.

## Measure the right outcomes

Watch quality issues, return reasons and support workload alongside review activity. Never invent a minimum number of reviews that guarantees sales or promise a specific star rating. Keep any programme-specific eligibility and cost claims tied to current official information before publishing them.

Explore [Ecomtik's account management service](/services/amazon-account-management) for a coordinated operational scope. For clearer product communication, read [the listing conversion guide](/blog/amazon-clicks-no-sales).

[^A10]: Amazon. [Amazon customer product review policies](https://sellercentral.amazon.com/gp/help/external/GYRKB5RU3FS5TURN)

# Amazon international expansion readiness checklist

Choose the next marketplace by the product's readiness and economics. A large audience is useful only if the business can supply, support and sell the product there. Amazon's Global Selling guidance distinguishes regional and country arrangements and highlights the operational work involved.[^A19]

Start with a short market comparison. Use evidence for demand, competition, expected net price, delivery cost and the team's ability to support customers.

## Confirm the seller and product route

Check registration eligibility for the actual business. Do not assume a new company is always required. Amazon explains that international businesses can sell to US customers through supported routes; a US LLC is not a universal prerequisite.[^A21]

Review product-category restrictions, documentation and destination requirements separately. For in-scope European products, the EU's General Product Safety Regulation needs appropriate consideration.[^R08] Other product-specific obligations may also apply. Use qualified local review for legal and tax requirements instead of treating a general launch checklist as clearance.

## Translate the buying decision

Localise the actual customer questions: measurements, compatibility, usage, included items and expectations. Literal translation can miss the phrases customers use when searching. Amazon Ads provides guidance on keyword targeting outside the US.[^A25]

Assign a competent language reviewer. Check product facts, search intent and advertising claims together. Do not imply local support in a language the team cannot service after the order.

## Calculate the destination economics

Model the expected selling price, product cost, transport, marketplace fees, fulfilment, returns, currency exposure and applicable taxes consistently. Identify which values are quotations and which are assumptions. Review the timing of cash payments as well as contribution per order.

For illustration, a product with a strong home-market margin might need different packaging and a more expensive return route abroad. The expansion decision should incorporate those changes before advertising begins. One successful marketplace does not establish the economics of another.

## Assign operational ownership

Decide who maintains listings, monitors stock, changes prices, reviews notices and answers customer-service questions. Document the fulfilment and return model. Amazon's Europe expansion guide explains relevant regional considerations, but programme eligibility and obligations must be checked for the seller's arrangement.[^A20]

Create a readiness record with a named owner, evidence and status for each dependency. Leave unresolved requirements visible. A launch date should follow the critical dependencies rather than conceal them.

## Run a controlled first release

Select a manageable product group with complete data and a clear replenishment plan. Agree what evidence would support expansion, what would require a change and what would stop the test. Use actual contribution, customer issues and operational capacity alongside sales.

Ecomtik's [marketplace expansion service](/services/global-marketplace-expansion) can be scoped around that decision and launch process. Before comparing countries, review [the launch-budget guide](/blog/amazon-launch-budget) and build the same cost model for each candidate.
